concepts: bouncing, elastic collision, path tracing, cyclic motion
description: The input is a black grid containing two fixed white squares on the left (one above center, one below) and a white circle on the right (all shapes keep their size and color).  To produce the output, simulate the circle’s horizontal motion under elastic collisions: it travels left until it hits the top square, reverses direction, then travels right to hit the bottom square, reverses again, and repeats this back-and-forth motion for four collisions in total.  As it moves, color every cell the circle passes through in yellow, leaving the background and the two squares unchanged.
visual_elements: two white squares on the left side (one above center, one below center)
one white circle on the right side (approximately center vertically)
static_patterns: positions of both white squares remain fixed
shapes (squares and circle) retain size and color throughout
dynamic_patterns: white circle travels horizontally from right toward the left squares
circle collides with a square and reverses its horizontal direction
circle moves back toward the opposite square, colliding and reversing again
repeated back-and-forth horizontal motion between the two squares
core_principles: Newton’s first law: an object in motion continues at constant velocity until acted upon by an external force
Elastic collision with a rigid barrier causes reversal of the object’s velocity vector
Reflection principle: angle (or direction) of motion in equals angle (or direction) of motion out
Cyclic repetition: the same motion sequence repeats after each collision
The most fundamental principle: an elastic collision with a rigid barrier reverses the moving object’s direction.
